content: The Rai staging system classifies chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) into five distinct stages. These stages are determined based on the degree of lymphocytosis (an abnormal increase in lymphocytes), hemoglobin levels, platelet counts, the presence of splenomegaly (enlargement of the spleen), and the presence of lymphadenopathy (enlargement of lymph nodes). The Binet staging system categorizes chronic lymphocytic leukemia into three stages. This classification is based on the degree of lymphocytosis, the presence of anemia or thrombocytopenia (low platelet count), and the involvement of three or more lymph node regions.
